content.title: About
content.content: Haupia is a traditional Hawaiian dessert made from coconut milk thickened with starch (usually corn starch). It has a delicate creamy coconut flavor, a light jelly‑like texture, and is typically served chilled.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Hawaiian word “haupia,” which simply means “coconut dessert.”
Traditionally the dessert was set in large wooden bowls and then cut into cubes.
In the United States haupia is often used as a filling for cakes, pastries, and ice cream.
Coconut milk, the main ingredient, is rich in lauric acid, giving it a distinctive aroma.
Haupia can be made gluten‑free by using tapioca or potato starch instead of wheat‑based thickeners.

items.title: Rich in medium‑chain triglycerides
items.content: Coconut milk contains MCTs that may support quick energy and metabolism.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: In modest amounts, coconut milk provides vitamin C, which helps the immune system.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Gluten‑ and lactose‑free
items.content: Haupia is suitable for people with celiac disease or lactose intolerance.

items.title: Low sugar when prepared accordingly
items.content: If only a small amount of sugar or a sugar substitute is used, the dessert remains moderately sweet.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut milk.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Coconut milk is high in saturated fat, so people with elevated cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: The dessert can be calorie‑dense, especially when sweetened.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Traditional recipes often call for a generous amount of sugar, which may be problematic for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve haupia chilled, cut into cubes or slices. It can be enjoyed on its own, used as a filling for cakes, pastries, ice cream, or incorporated into cocktails and fruit salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared haupia in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size containers for up to 2 months. Before serving, allow it to fully thaw and chill slightly.
